verdict.rationale: Codex's CLI docs say you can start it in a repository to explore unfamiliar code. The agent inspects files itself rather than needing hand-picked context, and subagents can split up a larger investigation. That covers the core of autonomous codebase exploration, but nothing documents mapping or explaining an entire codebase end to end. missing for 10: documented whole-repository mapping or architecture-summary capability, evidence of how context is gathered and managed across large codebases, independent hands-on corroboration of whole-codebase explanation quality.

support.subject: As a developer, I can have the agent map and explain an entire unfamiliar codebase without manually selecting context files

citations.quote: Start Codex in a repository to explore unfamiliar code, plan a change, edit files, and run your local development tools.
Let Codex inspect files, make edits, and run the tools already installed on your machine.
Split up a larger investigation — subagents: Ask Codex to delegate focused work to specialized agents, then bring their findings back into the main terminal session.
